title: The Effect of Remedial Program Practices on the Academic Performance of Slow Learners in Mathematics Subject in Public Lower-Day Secondary School in Rwanda: A Case of Kirehe District
extended_summary:
This study examines whether remedial program practices improve the academic performance of slow learners in mathematics in public lower-day secondary schools in Kirehe District, Rwanda. The paper focuses on whether remedial teaching helps students’ mathematical problem-solving abilities, whether performance changes before and after participation, and which program features are associated with better outcomes.

The intervention/approach studied is not a technology intervention but a school-based remedial education program. The authors examine several implementation features of remedial support, including teaching methods, session frequency, teacher-student ratio, curriculum alignment, and student participation. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and school-record performance information, using a mixed-methods descriptive survey design. Participants included mathematics teachers, head teachers, deputy heads of studies, and students from four public secondary schools in Kirehe District.

The study concludes that remedial practices are positively associated with stronger mathematics performance, including test scores, retention of mathematical concepts, and sustained academic improvement. Student participation emerged as the strongest predictor, followed by frequency of sessions and individualized attention in smaller groups. The authors recommend structured, needs-based remedial programs with frequent sessions, smaller teacher-student ratios, active engagement, and ongoing monitoring to support slow learners in mathematics.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed descriptive survey with mixed methods and correlational/regression analyses, not an experimental design. It provides useful observational evidence, but causal claims are limited by self-report data and the lack of random assignment or a clear comparison group.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported associations are positive and sometimes strong (e.g., r=0.701, r=0.728), but they come from a local sample of slow learners in four schools and do not establish causality. The impact is promising for a priority population, yet the generalizability and intervention certainty remain modest.

finding.finding_summary: The study reports that remedial program practices were associated with improved mathematical problem-solving and test performance among slow learners in public lower-day secondary schools in Kirehe District, Rwanda. Teacher perceptions showed high agreement that remedial teaching improved problem-solving (mean=4.33, SD=1.10; 83.32% agreed/strongly agreed), and student perceptions were even stronger (mean=4.76-4.93 across items). Correlational results showed a strong positive association between remedial teaching methods and mathematics test scores (r=0.701, p=0.002; n=90), and between remedial teaching methods and retention of mathematical concepts (r=0.728, p=0.001; n=90).
finding.measure: Mathematical problem-solving skills, mathematics test scores, retention of mathematical concepts

finding.finding_summary: The paper also substantively examines student participation and engagement as factors in remedial learning success. Active participation was strongly associated with sustained academic improvement (r=0.623, p=0.043; n=90), and student survey items on participation showed very high endorsement (e.g., mean=4.93 for participation improving problem-solving).
finding.measure: Student participation / engagement in remedial sessions
